page.title: AI Consultant vs Automation Agency Services Compared
page.description: Compare scope, pricing, deliverables and ownership so you can choose the right partner for AI workflows.
page.h1: AI consultant vs automation agency services
page.definition: AI consultant vs automation agency services are two engagement models for adding artificial intelligence to marketing, content or event operations. A consultant delivers strategy and a roadmap. An agency delivers working automations, integrations and ongoing support.
page.quick_answer: Choose a consultant when you need an assessment, prioritised use cases and a tool decision before building. Choose an agency when you have a clear use case and want production-ready workflows with a support retainer.

sections.h2: What does each partner actually deliver?

blocks.p: A consultant produces an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap. An agency produces working automations, integrations and documentation, often backed by a monthly support retainer.

ul: Consultant output: assessment, prioritised use-case list, tool choice, roadmap
Agency output: working automations, integrations, documentation, support retainer

blocks.p: Consultants typically charge a day rate or a fixed project fee. Agencies usually charge a fixed build fee plus a monthly retainer for maintenance and iteration.

head: Model
Typical Structure
rows: Day rate or fixed project fee
Fixed build fee plus monthly retainer

sections.h2: Which engagement fits my current maturity?

blocks.p: If you have not yet mapped processes or selected tools, a consultant helps you decide what to automate and with which platform. If you already know the workflow and need it built, an agency moves faster to a live system.

ol: Map current processes and pain points
Decide whether you need strategy first or build first
Match the partner model to that decision

sections.h2: Who owns the outcome after delivery?

blocks.p: With a consultant, your team owns implementation of the roadmap. With an agency, the agency often retains ownership of the automation layer and provides a support retainer for changes, monitoring and platform updates.

ul: Agency: agency often owns automation layer and provides retainer support

blocks.p: Some firms offer a discovery phase followed by a build phase under the same contract. Clarify whether the same people who write the roadmap also build the workflows, or whether handoffs introduce risk.

ul: Ask if discovery and build teams are the same people
Define handoff criteria and acceptance gates
Confirm who maintains the system after launch

faq.q: How long does a typical consultant assessment take?
faq.a: A focused assessment usually runs two to four weeks, covering stakeholder interviews, process mapping, tool evaluation and a prioritised roadmap with clear next steps.

faq.q: What should an agency build fee include?
faq.a: The build fee should cover workflow design, integration development, testing, documentation, a handoff session and a defined warranty period for bug fixes before the retainer starts.

faq.q: Do I need a consultant before hiring an agency?
faq.a: Not always. If you already have a documented process, approved tool stack and executive sign-off, you can engage an agency directly. A consultant adds value when those inputs are missing.

faq.q: What happens when the platform changes its API?
faq.a: Under a retainer, the agency monitors API changes and updates the automation. Without a retainer, your internal team must maintain the integration or pay for ad-hoc fixes.

faq.q: How do I measure ROI for either model?
faq.a: Track time saved per workflow, error reduction, volume handled without added headcount, and speed to launch new campaigns. Agree on baseline metrics before the engagement starts.
